bullets.text: The Plan is a placeholder.
The Plan accepts a plausible output without asserting the exact observable representation required by the task.
The Plan makes mixed known and unknown inputs entirely unevaluated, discarding reductions that are already provably safe.
The Plan prescribes an edit location without tracing the concrete call path that produces the incorrect result.
The Plan extends a serialized format without defining which legacy or new representation remains authoritative.
The Plan tests successful serialization round trips but not malformed data in every representation the new format retains.
The Plan's concrete predicate does not match the invariant it claims to implement.
The Plan generalizes behavior across an input category without testing a special value that changes the required output.
The Plan patches a downstream consumer without checking whether the producer's intermediate output already violates its contract.
The Plan changes a shared path but tests only the triggering input, omitting existing behavior on that path.
The Plan inspects type information only after a conversion that erases it.
The Plan quotes only the reported SQL identifier while leaving other interpolated identifiers in the same statement unquoted.
The Plan's SQL regression test makes only one interpolated identifier adversarial, leaving other identifier positions untested.
The planned interoperability fallback occurs after validation that can reject the foreign operand before delegation.
The Plan changes cooperative operator dispatch without testing foreign output operands.
The Plan equates conversion failure with dispatch incompatibility without preserving established errors when delegation is declined.
The Plan leaves an observable policy unresolved between alternatives requiring different implementations and tests.
The Plan preserves a legacy representation despite task evidence that the representation must change.
The Plan adds an early return that bypasses an existing helper without preserving its warnings and validation.
The Plan restores input dtypes by column name without excluding outputs whose values legitimately changed type.
The Plan adds a lower cutoff to a rule whose specification defines only a future cutoff.
The Plan's boundary tests mirror its proposed algorithm instead of independently encoding the specification's exact inequality.
The Plan derives a stronger API contract from an assertion whose boolean logic does not enforce that contract.
The Plan chooses a synthetic sentinel that can equal a real value despite representing a distinct state.
The Plan preserves a fabricated fallback for an accessor intended to mirror an optional value.
The Plan forwards a metadata option without tracing which input wins when several inputs provide metadata.
The Plan's metadata test does not assign distinguishable values to every candidate source.
The Plan defines metadata precedence only for array inputs, omitting the fallback when the preferred input is scalar.
The Plan adds inherited aggregation to a shared reader without preserving an own-object mode needed by local writers.
The Plan omits non-applicable per-item values, breaking an output attribute's required one-entry-per-item cardinality.
The Plan derives configuration keys from shorthand without checking the exact registered names.
